interpretations.title: Support is the cold part of the book
interpretations.finding: Support calls average 2.94 on the 1–5 score. External calls average 3.71. The gap is 0.77 points, and 59% of support calls sit on the negative side of the label.
interpretations.why_it_matters: A single company-wide sentiment number hides the motion that is actually struggling. Someone who only watches external calls will think the quarter feels fine while support is where customers describe the product failing.

interpretations.title: 2026-03 is the weak month
interpretations.finding: Mean sentiment moves from 3.83 in 2026-04 (38 meetings) to 2.78 in 2026-03 (36 meetings).
interpretations.why_it_matters: A trend only matters if someone can name the operating event underneath it. Pair this month with the incident cohort before treating it as a general mood shift.

interpretations.title: Incident-titled meetings are a different population
interpretations.finding: 10 meetings have an incident, outage, or war-room title. Their mean score is 2.18, versus 3.55 for the other 90. 49 meetings mention the outage in the title, summary, or topics and average 2.93.
interpretations.why_it_matters: The incident is not confined to the bridge calls. 39 additional meetings still talk about the outage in the summary or topics, including account reviews and support cases. A status-page postmortem will undercount that.

interpretations.title: The label is coarse. The score is the instrument.
interpretations.finding: 66 of 100 meetings are labeled mixed-positive or mixed-negative. The corpus mean is 3.42. Within a label the scores sit in a tight band, so the label is a readable bucket and the score is what you chart.
interpretations.why_it_matters: Do not build the dashboard on six sentiment names. Build it on the score, cut by call type and by the incident cohort, and use the label as a check that the score still means what the original model said it meant.

commentary: The source file ships 351 distinct topic labels across 100 meetings. 76% of those labels appear once. A label that appears once cannot be a category.
The governed taxonomy covers 100% of meetings and maps 58% of the raw labels. What it does not map stays visible as unclassified instead of being forced into a bucket.

Topics generated by lexical-nmf were fit on summaries and transcripts only, with the provided labels held out. Mean lexical overlap with the provided labels is 8%. That figure is a token diagnostic, not classification accuracy. The average governed theme lands in one generated topic 60% of the time. Zero shared words is marked review recommended. A low non-zero score is expected, because labels are phrases and the model emits content words, and is not an error.

Publish the governed themes. Keep the raw labels as evidence under each theme. Review zero-overlap meetings before anyone treats a generated topic name as a product category. That is the governance loop: a stable taxonomy, an independent model, and a human on the disagreements.

topic_examples.selection_rule: For each governed theme, keep meetings whose primary theme is that theme. Sort by the number of provided labels that match the theme keywords, descending; then by the governed theme score, descending; then by lexical overlap, descending; then by meeting_id, ascending. Keep at most two. A theme with fewer meetings contributes only those meetings. Nothing is invented. The evidence excerpt is the first transcript sentence that contains a matched theme keyword, otherwise the first summary sentence. Email addresses and phone numbers are redacted and the excerpt is capped at 240 characters.
topic_examples.lexical_overlap_note: lexical_topic_overlap is the Jaccard overlap between tokens in the provided topic labels and tokens in the held-out model's topic terms. JSON still stores the same number as topic_agreement. The score is a lexical diagnostic, not calibrated classification accuracy. Zero shared content words is shown as review recommended. A low non-zero score is expected and is not treated as an error.

notes: Coverage 86%: 100/100 meetings land in a governed theme (100%), 4/4 stakeholders have a finding, and 19 meetings are cited as evidence.
Consistency 100%: 10/10 non-adjacent sentiment labels keep their score order, and the published call-type means match a fresh average (100%).
Actionability 100%: 9/9 insights include a number, a reason to care, a recommendation, and at least one cited meeting.
Confidence 100%: sample factor 100% at 100 meetings, smallest call-type cell 27, mean evidence items 3.0.

The composite scores the briefing's structure: themes assigned, labels consistent with scores, insights written so a person can act. It does not measure whether a reviewer would accept the conclusion. That is the human loop described below.
quality.next_evolution: The next evolution is a human-in-the-loop review on the zero-overlap topics and on every insight. A reviewer approves, corrects, or marks a category ambiguous, and accepts, rejects, or sends a finding back. Those saved decisions are the evaluation set. An LLM is not a substitute for that file. This score is the stand-in until those decisions exist.

method.architecture: Folders become Meeting objects in one loader. Feature extraction, topic analysis, sentiment analysis, and insight generation only see that object. The dashboard, the charts, and this report are consumers of the pipeline output, not readers of the raw JSON.
method.categorization: Categories are a governed taxonomy mapped from the provided topic labels, audited by a topic model (lexical-nmf) fit on the summary and transcript with those labels held out. Raw labels stay attached as evidence. The model behind the audit is swappable: lexical NMF is the default, BERTopic implements the same TopicModel contract.
method.sentiment: Meeting scores and labels are used as recorded. Turns carry their own polarity and are rolled up by call type. The writing around the charts is generated from the gaps, so a different corpus produces a different sentence rather than a fixed March-outage story.
method.governance: Most provided labels appear once. Publishing them as categories would look precise and be unstable. The review queue is the set of meetings where the governed theme and the generated topic share no tokens.
method.extensibility: A new analytic implements Analyzer.analyze(meetings) and is called from the runner. A new stakeholder is a function that returns Insights. A new consumer reads report.json. None of those changes should reopen the loader.
method.consumption: Support, product, engineering, and sales read different sections of one report. They share evidence ids, so a quote in the sales book can be opened as the same meeting a support leader is already looking at.

label_inventory.note: Each meeting summary ships free-text topic labels. Those strings are evidence. A label that appears once is not a category.

methodology.governed_mapping: The published categories are a fixed theme list. A provided label that contains a theme keyword adds 2 to that theme. A keyword in the title or summary adds 0.5. The highest score is the primary theme. Labels that match nothing do not invent a theme. Meetings with no positive score stay unclassified.
methodology.held_out_discovery: A second pass fits lexical-nmf on the summary plus transcript sentences. Provided topic labels are not in that text. Speaker-name tokens are stopped so the model does not cluster people. The lexical default uses TF-IDF (unigrams and bigrams) and NMF with 8 components and random_state 7.
methodology.why_this_corpus: The corpus is about 100 meetings. TF-IDF + NMF with a fixed seed is deterministic, has no extra model download, and can be refit in the same pipeline that writes the briefing. Embedding models move around on a corpus this small, so they are not the default audit.
methodology.bertopic: BERTopic implements the same TopicModel contract and is selected with --topic-model bertopic. It clusters embedding neighborhoods and can mark outliers. It is optional because this corpus is small, the dependency is heavy, and the briefing needs a repeatable audit rather than a second taxonomy. It does not replace the governed themes.
methodology.lexical_overlap: lexical_topic_overlap is the Jaccard overlap between tokens in the provided topic labels and tokens in the held-out model's topic terms. JSON still stores the same number as topic_agreement. The score is a lexical diagnostic, not calibrated classification accuracy. Zero shared content words is shown as review recommended. A low non-zero score is expected and is not treated as an error.
methodology.sentiment: Source-provided meeting score: summary.json sentimentScore, scale 1–5. The analyzer copies it and does not change it.
not_measured: Classification accuracy, until a person saves adjudicated rows in review_decisions.json. The pipeline does not fill those rows, and a blank file stays not yet available.
A new sentiment model. Meeting scores are the source 1–5 values, unchanged.
Causal effect of the March outage on support sentiment. The time cut is descriptive.
Revenue, bookings, or a churn forecast. The win/loss figure, when cited, is what an internal call recorded.
Whether a stakeholder accepts an insight, until that person records accept or reject. Needs revision and needs more evidence are not acceptance. The quality composite scores briefing structure only.

review_queue.instructions: Record decisions in review_decisions.json. Accept, edit, or reject. An edit must name corrected_theme for a meeting item. A reason is free text. This queue is regenerated from the pipeline. It does not store decisions and it does not modify source meetings.

topic_examples.selection_rule: For each governed theme, keep meetings whose primary theme is that theme. Sort by the number of provided labels that match the theme keywords, descending; then by the governed theme score, descending; then by lexical overlap, descending; then by meeting_id, ascending. Keep at most two. A theme with fewer meetings contributes only those meetings. Nothing is invented. The evidence excerpt is the first transcript sentence that contains a matched theme keyword, otherwise the first summary sentence. Email addresses and phone numbers are redacted and the excerpt is capped at 240 characters.
topic_examples.lexical_overlap_note: lexical_topic_overlap is the Jaccard overlap between tokens in the provided topic labels and tokens in the held-out model's topic terms. JSON still stores the same number as topic_agreement. The score is a lexical diagnostic, not calibrated classification accuracy. Zero shared content words is shown as review recommended. A low non-zero score is expected and is not treated as an error.
